NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event. Sandeep claimed the men's 400m T64 title, while Haney won gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 event.India also added silver medals through Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan, Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in the women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. The contingent is chasing its best-ever Asian Para Games haul of 108 medals, achieved at Hangzhou in 2023.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan wins gold and two silver medals at Asian Para Games 2026. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

Article Title: Mona Agarwal wins gold, becomes first Indian to win Asian Para Games medal in 50m rifle 3 positions
Article Text:
Mona Agarwal (Image credit: X)

Mona outguns Chinese rival as Avani misses podium

Second gold after opening-day triumph

India close in on best-ever Asian Para Games medal tally

India's Mona Agarwal continued her golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, rewriting the world record to clinch her second gold medal of the competition in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final on Friday. The Indian para shooter produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, setting a new World Record and Asian Para Games Record.Mona's latest triumph came after she had already struck gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.Mona delivered a composed performance in the 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final to secure the gold medal with a world-record score of 357.5. China's Cuiping Zhang finished second to take silver, trailing the Indian by 3.8 points.India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara , narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth. Avani had been among the leading contenders after the prone position but lost ground during the standing series, which proved decisive in the final standings.Mona had earlier teamed up with Avani for an Indian one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.She won gold with a score of 250 after the seventh series, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Mona's second gold came as India continued their push to surpass their previous best performance at the Asian Para Games. At the time of reporting, India had collected 103 medals: 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze and stood fourth in the overall standings, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India's record haul at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games was 111 medals.
Article Summary: India's Mona Agarwal wins second gold of 2026 Asian Para Games. She produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang. India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara, narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth.

Article Title: Asian Para Games 2026: Harvinder Singh, Vijay Sundi strike gold in men's recurve doubles
Article Text:
Indian para archers Harvinder Singh, left, and Vijay Sundi (Image: PTI)

India's Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi delivered a composed performance under pressure to clinch the gold medal in the men's para recurve doubles event at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games on Friday, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final. The Indian duo held their nerve in a closely contested battle at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square, winning the final two sets by narrow margins to secure the top podium finish.After sharing the opening set 35-35, Harvinder and Vijay edged the second set 37-36 before producing another crucial effort to take the third 38-36. Their consistency in the decisive moments proved the difference as India secured another gold medal in para archery.The victory marked a significant achievement for the Indian pair, who maintained their composure against the Chinese challenge to seal the title with a 5-1 scoreline on set points.India's Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan, meanwhile, had to settle for silver in the women's para recurve doubles event after suffering a 0-6 defeat against China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian in the final.The Indian pair struggled to match their opponents' scoring consistency, losing all three sets 31-38, 30-35 and 29-39 at the Okazaki venue.
Article Summary: India's Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi clinch gold medal in men's para recurve doubles event at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games. Article Title: Asian Para Games: Thulasimathi clinches silver in women's singles SU5, remains in contention for two more golds
Article Text:
Thulasimathi Murugesan

Thulasimathi falls short against Yang after impressive semi-final comeback

Two more gold medal opportunities await

Who is Thulasimathi Murugesan?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. She will look to make amends in the remaining finals as India aim to add to their medal tally.Thulasimathi, currently ranked World No. 2, could not overcome Yang in the title clash, with the Chinese player securing the gold medal in straight games. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Nitesh and Thulasimathi prevailed 21-19, 14-21, 21-17 to secure their place in the gold medal match.Later, Thulasimathi will team up with Manasi Girishchandra Joshi in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 final. The Indian pair will face China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian, giving Thulasimathi another opportunity to challenge for gold against the Chinese shuttler who defeated her in the singles final.Born on April 11, 2002, in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, Thulasimathi has established herself as one of India's leading para-badminton players. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. In recognition of her achievements in para-badminton, including her Paralympic success, she was also honoured with the Arjuna Award.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan won silver in the women's singles SU5 event. The 24-year- old lost to China's Yang Qiuxia 18-21, 11-21 in the final. She is still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events.

Article Title: Jude Bellingham hailed for ‘absolute class act’ after stopping male journalist from interrupting female reporter in chaotic Real Madrid interview
Article Text:
Jude Bellingham praised for defending BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway after she was interrupted during Real Madrid’s 5-1 win over PSV.

Bellingham steps in after BBC reporter is interrupted

Elizabeth Conway explains the pressure of interviewing at Real Madrid

Bellingham's stunning goal earns praise from Mourinho and Valverde

Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham celebrates after scoring his side's second goal during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Real Madrid and PSV in Madrid, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Daily Mail Sport

Jude Bellingham had just scored what he described as the best goal of his life, but one of his most widely praised moments after Real Madrid's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV had nothing to do with football. The England midfielder stopped a male reporter from interrupting BBC journalist Elizabeth Conway, insisting she be allowed to finish her question in a crowded mixed zone at the Bernabeu.Bellingham was in considerable demand after coming off the bench to help Real Madrid beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday. His outstanding volley had put Madrid ahead, while he later provided the assist for Vinicius Jr 's fifth goal, giving reporters plenty to ask about after the final whistle.BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway was among those waiting to speak to the midfielder in the mixed zone, where journalists gather behind a barrier to interview players as they leave the pitch. She had asked Bellingham about the goal when another reporter interrupted her attempt to ask a second question.Bellingham immediately intervened.“Sorry, she's got one more,” he said, pointing towards Conway and making clear that she should be allowed to continue.The journalist then asked whether Bellingham felt he was playing the best football of his career for both club and country.“My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one.Your last one doesn't really matter,” he replied.“Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.”Conway later shared the exchange on Instagram, writing: “Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,” alongside a handshake emoji. The clip quickly circulated online, with supporters praising the midfielder for his consideration.BBC presenter Kelly Somers was among those who responded, writing: “So lovely he did this to you @elizabeth.conway_ and well done for also standing your ground.”The BBC Football account also joined in, joking: “Jude Bellingham with his second assist of the night.”Conway subsequently discussed the incident on BBC Radio WM, explaining why Bellingham's intervention meant so much in an environment she described as intimidating.The mixed zone at the Bernabeu can become particularly chaotic when a high-profile player stops to speak to the media. Journalists compete for space around the barrier, with microphones, cameras and reporters often crowding one another in an effort to secure an interview.“It is utter carnage,” Conway said.“Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust.“You've got elbows you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.“I'm one of very, very, few female reporters and one of very, very, few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so important.”Conway explained that interruptions were commonplace and that reporters were expected to compete aggressively for the opportunity to ask questions. In a separate video shared online, she described how being shorter than many of the journalists around her meant she needed to position herself directly at the front of the barrier.“Because I’m short, I have to get right at the front of the barrier to have any chance. I was right at the front underneath Jude’s chin,” she said.“It’s normal protocol, at least at Real Madrid, that journalists just throw in questions. There are no niceties or politeness; it’s everyone out for themselves.”She particularly appreciated that Bellingham had noticed the interruption and deliberately made room for her to continue.“It was so nice,” she said, adding that the gesture showed him being “respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist”.“It was especially appreciated because I am one of so few female journalists at Real Madrid, and one of the very few English journalists,” she added.The exchange came after a performance that had already made Bellingham the centre of attention at the Bernabeu. Introduced from the bench, the 23-year-old produced a remarkable finish to put Real Madrid in front against PSV.After collecting a loose ball around 25 yards from goal, he controlled it with his left foot before flicking it into the air with his right and striking a volley with the outside of the same boot. The ball flew into the far corner, leaving PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar with little chance.Bellingham was asked what had gone through his mind during the finish.“Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,” he said. “I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.“It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it.“It was a nice goal and important for the team being the second goal and gave us control.”He was even more emphatic when asked to rank the strike among his previous goals.“I think this was the best goal of my life,” he declared.Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho was equally impressed, explaining how Bellingham had changed the team's performance after his introduction.“Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,” Mourinho said. “He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.”Bellingham's brother Jobe, meanwhile, had his own reaction to the goal after featuring for Borussia Dortmund in their 1-1 draw against Arsenal on the same evening. He jokingly suggested the shot had “come off his shin” before conceding that it was a “great goal”.The performance also came amid growing attention over Bellingham's future at Real Madrid.reported on November 24 that the England international was in advanced discussions over a contract extension until 2031, with negotiations having begun in September.His existing deal runs until 2029 and is understood to be worth approximately £12.5 million a year after tax. Madrid are keen to reward his performances with improved terms, potentially bringing his salary in line with team-mate Vinicius Jr, whose contract extension last summer was reportedly worth around £500,000 a week after tax.Sources at the Spanish club were said to be confident that an agreement was approaching. For now, however, Bellingham's intervention in the mixed zone has given supporters another reason to praise a player whose influence on the night extended well beyond his remarkable goal.
Article Summary: Jude Bellingham defended BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway after she was interrupted during Real Madrid’s 5-1 win over PSV. The England midfielder stopped a male reporter from interrupting Conway, insisting she be allowed to finish her question. The clip quickly circulated online, with supporters praising the midfielder for his consideration. Bellingham was in considerable demand after coming off the bench to help Real Madrid beat PSV Eindhoven.

Article Title: Just 3 months after moving to US, Indian-origin English footballer Krissh Mahatma, 18, shot dead outside Mississippi restaurant
Article Text:
18-year-old footballer Krissh Mahatma shot dead in Mississippi, with a 22-year-old suspect arrested and charged with murder/ Image: Instagram

Krissh Mahatma shot dead outside Mississippi restaurant

From London football to a new life with the Co-Lin Wolves

Family, college and restaurant owner respond to tragedy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Krissh Mahatma had moved from London to the United States to pursue a football career and was only three months into his first season with the Co-Lin Wolves when his life was cut short. The 18-year-old striker was shot dead outside a taco restaurant in Jackson, Mississippi, after an argument involving a group of people reportedly escalated into gunfire. A 22-year-old man has since been arrested and charged with murder Mahatma was fatally shot at approximately 3.39am on Sunday outside Green Ghost Tacos, a popular restaurant in downtown Jackson. The establishment was closed at the time, and the shooting reportedly took place in a parking lot across the street as Mahatma and a group of people were leaving the area, according to sources who spoke to local broadcaster WLBT The London-born footballer had been with teammates from Copiah-Lincoln Community College, where he played for the Co-Lin Wolves. Witnesses told Dark Horse Press that the group noticed an intoxicated man outside the restaurant and offered to give him a lift home. The offer allegedly led to an argument, which escalated into a physical confrontation before the man produced a firearm and fired at the group.Mahatma was struck by a bullet and taken to a nearby hospital in a private vehicle, where he was pronounced dead, according to Hinds County Coroner Jeramiah Howard, as reported by WLBT.The Mississippi Department of Public Safety has not provided further details about what prompted the confrontation.Capitol Police subsequently arrested Danny Luna, 22, and charged him with murder. Police Chief Mark Miller acknowledged the arrest while recognising the loss suffered by Mahatma's family“While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognize that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one,” Miller said, offering his “thoughts and prayers” to Mahatma's “family and loved ones”.The investigation is ongoing, and the circumstances surrounding the fatal confrontation have not been fully established by authorities.Mahatma was a freshman at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Wesson, approximately 45 miles south of Jackson. He played as a forward, wore the No. 11 shirt and had joined the college's soccer programme after previously representing Watford 'A' in England's post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league.Co-Lin announced his signing in February with a graphic welcoming him to the team and the message: “Welcome to the Wolfpack, Krissh.”He had made 14 appearances during his first three months with the Wolves, scoring once. His goal came in September, during a 3-2 victory over National Park College.The college community paid tribute following news of his death, with Co-Lin president Dewayne Middleton expressing the institution's grief.“Copiah-Lincoln Community College is mourning the loss of freshman soccer player Krissh Mahatma. Krissh will be deeply missed by his teammates and the entire Co-Lin family,” Middleton said in a statement.Mahatma had moved across the Atlantic only months earlier to continue his education and develop his football career. His death has left teammates, coaches and those who had welcomed him to the college community mourning a young player whose time in the United States had only just begun. fundraiser established to support Mahatma's family described the loss of a young man who had left home to begin a new chapter of his life.“He was just beginning a new chapter of life far away from home,” the fundraiser said.“His sudden passing has left his family, friends, teammates, coaches, and the entire Co-Lin soccer community heartbroken.“Behind this tragedy is a family grieving the loss of their son and loved ones trying to make sense of a loss that feels impossible to put into words.”Green Ghost Tacos also issued a statement after the shooting, offering condolences while clarifying that the restaurant was not open or conducting business when the incident occurred. The owner said:“On behalf of the entire Green Ghost family, I extend my deepest and most heartfelt condolences to the family, friends, loved ones, and university community mourning the tragic loss of a young student. Our hearts are heavy, and our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by this devastating incident.“While this tragedy occurred near our establishment, we would like to clarify that Green Ghost was closed and was not conducting business at the time of the shooting.“The safety and well-being of our patrons, employees, and surrounding community remain a top priority. We are committed to cooperating fully with law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident.“Out of respect for the grieving family and the investigation, we will refrain from speculating or commenting further on the details at this time.“Above all, we recognize that a family has suffered an unimaginable loss. We ask that the community join us in extending compassion, prayers, and support to those affected during this incredibly difficult time.”Mahatma's death has left his family grieving in England and his teammates in Mississippi mourning a player who had travelled thousands of miles to pursue his ambitions. He was 18.
Article Summary: Krissh Mahatma was shot dead outside a taco restaurant in Jackson, Mississippi. The 18-year-old had moved from London to the United States to pursue a football career. He was only three months into his first season with the Co-Lin Wolves when his life was cut short. Danny Luna, 22, has been arrested and charged with murder.
